name: Height
team_execution_depth: Before shutdown, Height was a credible team-execution tool that combined task tracking and chat in one surface — tasks, subtasks, custom attributes, lists, sprints, dependencies, and sophisticated automation. The unique angle was that chat threads were native to tasks, so daily standups, blocker discussions, and decisions sat inside the work item rather than in a separate Slack channel. The execution layer was praised by product and engineering teams for flexibility, design quality, and feature completeness. As of September 24, 2025 the service is discontinued and all data was deleted, so what remains is the design pattern and lessons, not a usable tool.
keyboard_command_ux: Height shipped a Cmd+K command bar and keyboard-first workflows that drew explicit comparison to Linear; status changes, list switching, and task creation were keyboard-driven. The DNA was strongly fluency-rewarding. [uncertain] Specific shortcut documentation is no longer maintained since the shutdown.
ui_responsiveness: Height was widely described as snappy and well-designed, in the Linear/Notion design tier rather than the Jira/legacy tier. [uncertain] No public P50/P95 benchmarks; reputational evidence only, and the product is now offline.
real_time_collaboration: This was Height's signature capability and the reason it is referenced in the brief. Threaded chat lived on every task and inside every list, blurring the line between Slack and the work item. @mentions, presence, live cursors on docs, and inline replies meant that the 'open Slack to ask a quick question about this ticket' switch was largely eliminated. The Copilot Chat feature (launched 2024) added an AI participant in those threads that could summarise, suggest assignees, dedupe tasks, turn chat messages into subtasks, and auto-generate async standups. This is the model the brief flags as relevant to EAP's missing real-time collaboration story.
mobile_experience: Height shipped iOS and Android apps with task view/edit and chat. [uncertain] Specific sprint board parity and offline capability details are no longer documented since the shutdown.
in_tool_documentation: Tasks supported rich descriptions and attachments, and Pages/specs lived alongside tasks. The 'auto-updating specifications' Copilot feature kept doc-style specs synchronised with task progress — an early version of the docs-as-planning idea Notion now sells. This closed-loop pattern is part of why the brief calls Height a relevant reference for context-switching reduction.
developer_experience: GitHub, GitLab, Slack, Figma, Sentry, Linear-style integrations existed. Branch/PR linking on tasks was supported. [uncertain] Native IDE plugin (VS Code, JetBrains) presence is not clearly documented; CLI was not a headline feature. Developer feel was 'beautifully designed task tracker with chat' rather than 'tool that lives inside the editor'.
vcs_integration_depth: GitHub two-way linking on tasks with PR status reflected on cards. [uncertain] Depth of auto-state-transitions on PR open/merge, branch-naming enforcement, and deployment status are not now retrievable from a maintained doc set.
ai_agentic_maturity: Height was an early mover. Copilot Chat (announced 2024) embedded a GPT-class assistant in every task thread. The product later pivoted to 'fully autonomous AI workflows throughout every stage of the project management process', covering bug triage, backlog pruning, auto-updating specs, dedup, smart assignee suggestion, subtask extraction from chat, and async standup generation. The model was generative-plus-agentic before the term 'agentic' was common. It pre-dated MCP, so there is no native MCP endpoint on record. [uncertain] Whether Height shipped an MCP server before shutdown is not confirmed.
time_to_value: Height was a fast-onboarding tool — sign up, import or create lists, start chatting. Lower configuration burden than Jira; less template scaffolding than Notion or ClickUp. Closer to Linear's 'open it and use it' ergonomics.
migration_story: Critical point for the brief: Height shut down September 24, 2025 and deleted all customer data after the shutdown. Users had to export to JSON or CSV before that date. ClickUp's import tool can process Height exports, and Shortcut published a Height migration guide. Linear is the closest spiritual successor by feel; Asana, Jira, and Notion are also documented receivers. The migration story is now retrospective only.
deprecation_transition_risk: Maximum — the product is discontinued. Service ended September 24, 2025 (announced March 22, 2025 by CEO Michaël Villar). Founders did not publicly disclose reasons; Height was not acquired. Total funding was $18.3M raised across 3.5 years of public availability. For the purposes of this research it is a teardown reference, not a competitive option.
safe_framework_alignment: None of substance. Height was a flat team-and-product tool. No PI Planning, no ART, no Capability/Feature SAFe taxonomy, no cross-ART dependency mapping, no WSJF. It was never positioned at this layer.
reporting_metrics: Lists, filters, and basic burndown/velocity for sprints. Reporting was not Height's headline strength. [uncertain] Specific built-in chart inventory is no longer published.
customer_signal_ingestion: Native chat threads on tasks plus Slack/email-to-task automations meant customer-facing teams could route signal into work items. Not a Productboard-class capability (no NPS, no native feature voting), but better than most peers because of the chat-native surface.
integration_ecosystem: GitHub, GitLab, Slack, Figma, Sentry, Zapier, plus webhooks and a public API. Marketplace was small relative to Jira; depth was solid for product/engineering core stack. [uncertain] Current integration list is moot post-shutdown.
community_vitality: Mid-tier in life. Reasonable Twitter/X presence, design-conscious user base. Smaller than Linear's community, larger than niche tools. Now zero — the company and product are offline. Some user-generated 'lessons from Height' retrospectives circulating in 2025-2026.
self_hosting_data_residency: SaaS-only. No self-hosted or private-cloud option was ever offered. EU data residency is not on record. [uncertain] Whether enterprise customers had any regional hosting election is not surfaced.
customization: Custom attributes, custom task types, custom views, automation rules, sophisticated 'adaptive workflow' engine that surfaced relevant fields based on task type. Lighter-touch than Jira's schema-everything model; more flexible than Linear's opinionated rigidity. Praised for hitting a middle ground.
pricing_commercial_model: Per-seat SaaS. List rate was around $6.99/user/month at the time of shutdown — directly competitive with ClickUp ($7) and below Linear ($8-14). Free tier existed. No published per-portfolio or consumption tier.
total_cost_of_ownership: Was low — pure SaaS, low admin overhead, no implementation consultancy ecosystem. The TCO point that matters now is the exit cost: every Height customer paid a forced migration cost in 2025, which is a cautionary tale for any single-vendor lock-in in this category.
market_perception: While operating: 'cult favourite of product teams', often paired with Linear in 'modern alternatives to Jira' lists, design-press darling, regular Product Hunt visibility. Post-shutdown: a case study in the AI project management category — frequently cited as 'the pioneer that couldn't sustain the burn rate even after pivoting to autonomous AI'. Symbolic of the consolidation pressure on category 3 (chat-native PM) startups in the post-ZIRP era.
gaps_vs_market_leader: Versus Jira: no SAFe, no portfolio, marketplace orders of magnitude smaller, no enterprise admin/governance depth. Versus Linear: less polished P50 perceived latency, smaller community, weaker brand. Versus its own future: business viability — the defining gap. The lesson for EAP is not Height's competitive gaps but its design choices: chat-native task threads, AI-on-tasks, async standup auto-generation, dedup, and the 'one surface for execution and conversation' model.
